title: Update full drug list dataset and add verification that additions/updates apply correctly

requirements.text: Update the application’s curated drug dataset so the complete drug list is up to date and includes missing entries as needed, ensuring every drug record includes at minimum: name, status (approved/banned), date, category (when known), description, source, and safetyInfo.

quotes: update the entire list and make it up-to-date, and after that do a verification so everything add and update correctly
add and update the entire drug list

acceptanceCriteria: `frontend/src/data/curatedDrugDataset.ts` contains the updated complete dataset (no build/type errors).
All entries in the dataset conform to the `Drug` type (including valid `DrugStatus` and `DrugSource` variants).
Duplicate drug names are deterministically deduplicated using the existing `deduplicateDrugs` utility rules (banned > approved; newer date > older date).

requirements.text: Ensure backend drug query methods return complete datasets (no truncation): `getAllDrugs` returns all approved + banned drugs, and filtered endpoints (approved/banned) return the full correctly filtered lists, independent of any user profile state.

quotes: update the entire list and make it up-to-date, and after that do a verification so everything add and update correctly
add and update the entire drug list

acceptanceCriteria: Calling the backend drug-list query used by `useGetAllDrugs()` returns a list whose length matches the authoritative stored drug table size (no missing tail items).
Approved-only and banned-only results exactly match filtering by `DrugStatus` over the full stored list.
Results are stable across refreshes and do not depend on any profile loading state in the frontend.

requirements.text: Add a verification workflow that runs after a drug-list refresh/update to confirm that adds and updates were applied correctly, and expose the verification result to the UI.

quotes: after that do a verification so everything add and update correctly

acceptanceCriteria: A single user action (or existing refresh action) triggers: (1) update/refresh of the drug dataset and (2) a verification step.
Verification checks at minimum: total count > 0, no empty `name` values, no invalid/missing `status`, and no duplicate drugs when normalized by the same rules used in the curated dataset.
The UI shows a clear success/failure outcome for verification, and on failure provides a human-readable summary (English) of what failed (e.g., duplicate count, invalid entries count).

requirements.text: Update the Drug Database UI to reliably render the entire corresponding dataset in the All Drugs / Approved / Banned tabs, with client-side search/category filters applied to the full list (not a partially loaded subset). If the list is large, implement a UI strategy (pagination or virtualization) that still allows viewing the full list while preserving existing search, CSV export, and the drug details modal.

quotes: update the entire list and make it up-to-date, and after that do a verification so everything add and update correctly

acceptanceCriteria: The Drug Database module renders all items returned by the backend for each tab (All/Approved/Banned), without silently dropping items due to performance limits.
Search and category filtering operate over the full fetched dataset.
CSV export includes all currently filtered rows (not just the visible subset, if pagination/virtualization is used).
Drug details modal continues to open and display details for any item in the dataset.

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor in `backend/main.mo` (no additional canisters/services).
Do not edit any files under `frontend/src/components/ui` (compose existing components only).
Do not modify immutable frontend hook entrypoints: `frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts` / `.tsx`, `frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts`, `frontend/src/main.tsx`.
Use English for any new user-facing UI text.
nonGoals: Adding third-party authentication providers (only Internet Identity is supported).
Integrating external databases or non-Internet-Computer storage backends.
Building real-time features (WebSockets/push) for drug list updates.
